subject: english
prompt_en: Why did the fox call the raven 'Sir' and say the birds of the woods would call him 'King'?
prompt_hi: Fox ne raven ko 'Sir' kyun bola, aur kyun kaha ki jungle ke birds use 'King' bulayenge?
answer: To flatter him and make him proud, so that he would open his beak to sing and drop the food

subject: english
prompt_en: Stop after the fox asks the raven to sing. Predict what the raven will do, and what will happen to the morsel.
prompt_hi: Yahaan ruko, jab fox raven ko gaane ko kehta hai. Predict karo: raven kya karega, aur morsel ka kya hoga?
answer: He will open his beak to sing (croak), the morsel will fall, and the fox will take it

subject: english
prompt_en: A: Your art teacher says, 'The colours in your sky are lovely.' B: A classmate says, 'You are the greatest artist in the world! Now give me your new crayons.' Which one is flattery, and how do you know?
prompt_hi: A: Art teacher kehti hain, 'The colours in your sky are lovely.' B: Ek classmate kehta hai, 'You are the greatest artist in the world! Now give me your new crayons.' Kaunsa flattery hai, aur kaise pata?
answer: B, because it exaggerates and the speaker wants something (the crayons)

subject: english
prompt_en: Your younger brother thinks the fox was just being kind. Explain the poem's idea to him in two sentences.
prompt_hi: Tumhara chhota bhai sochta hai ki fox bas achha ban raha tha. Use do sentences mein poem ka idea samjhao.
answer: The fox was not kind; he praised the raven only to get his food. Do not be fooled by sweet words, and do not let pride make you foolish.

subject: english
prompt_en: 'The raven sat perched on a limb.' What is a limb of a tree?
prompt_hi: 'The raven sat perched on a limb.' Ped ka 'limb' kya hota hai?
answer: a branch

subject: english
prompt_en: Give the opposite of 'foolish' and the opposite of 'pride'.
prompt_hi: 'Foolish' ka opposite batao, aur 'pride' ka opposite bhi.
answer: wise; humility

subject: english
prompt_en: Mr Raven is male. Find and fix the mistake: 'The fox told the raven that you are a very fine bird.'
prompt_hi: Mr Raven male hai. Galti dhoondo aur theek karo: 'The fox told the raven that you are a very fine bird.'
answer: The fox told the raven that he was a very fine bird.

subject: english
prompt_en: Mr Raven is male. Find the mistake: 'The raven opened her beak and the food fell down.'
prompt_hi: Mr Raven male hai. Galti dhoondo: 'The raven opened her beak and the food fell down.'
answer: 'her' should be 'his': 'The raven opened his beak'

subject: english
prompt_en: In Hindi we say 'chikni-chupdi baatein' for sweet, false talk used to please someone. Which English word is closest?
prompt_hi: Hindi mein 'chikni-chupdi baatein' kehte hain, jab koi kuch paane ke liye meethi-meethi jhoothi baatein karta hai. English mein sabse paas ka word kaunsa hai?
answer: flattery

subject: english
prompt_en: A pop-up in an online game says: 'You're a genius player! Enter your parent's phone number to claim your prize.' How is this like the fox and the raven, and what should you do?
prompt_hi: Online game mein ek pop-up aata hai: 'You're a genius player! Enter your parent's phone number to claim your prize.' Ye fox aur raven jaisa kaise hai, aur tumhe kya karna chahiye?
answer: It flatters you to get something (the number), like the fox; do not type anything, close it and tell a parent

subject: english
prompt_en: Put these in order: (a) The thief hid inside, waiting for the couple to sleep. (b) The wife heard a strange noise. (c) The wife called 'Rama!' very loudly. (d) Rama the kotwal arrested the thief.
prompt_hi: In events ko sahi order mein lagao: (a) The thief hid inside, waiting for the couple to sleep. (b) The wife heard a strange noise. (c) The wife called 'Rama!' very loudly. (d) Rama the kotwal arrested the thief.
answer: b, a, c, d

subject: english
prompt_en: Why did the couple talk about naming a baby 'Rama' instead of just shouting 'Thief!'?
prompt_hi: Couple ne seedha 'Thief!' chillane ke bajaay baby ka naam 'Rama' rakhne ki baat kyun ki?
answer: So the thief would not know they were calling for help; calling 'Rama' louder and louder brought the kotwal while the thief thought it was a silly game

subject: english
prompt_en: The thief wished the couple would stop their 'silly game' and talk about their money. What did the thief think they were doing?
prompt_hi: Thief chahta tha ki couple apna 'silly game' band karein aur paison ki baat karein. Thief ke hisaab se couple kya kar rahe the?
answer: Just chatting about a name for their child; he did not know they were calling the kotwal

subject: english
prompt_en: The wife says that if the boy is out in the street, she will call out very loudly. Predict who will hear her and what will happen next.
prompt_hi: Wife kehti hai ki agar ladka street mein ho, toh woh bahut zor se bulayegi. Predict karo: kaun sunega, aur aage kya hoga?
answer: Rama the kotwal will hear his name, come to the house and catch the thief

subject: english
prompt_en: Couple A screams and runs at the thief in the dark. Couple B stays calm, plays a clever trick and gets the kotwal to come. Which couple is like the one in the story, and why is it safer?
prompt_hi: Couple A andhere mein cheekhte hue thief pe toot padta hai. Couple B shaant rehta hai, chaalaaki se kotwal ko bula leta hai. Story jaisa kaunsa hai, aur woh safe kyun hai?
answer: Couple B, because staying calm and getting the kotwal is safer than fighting a thief in the dark

subject: english
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child what 'Rama to the Rescue' teaches about facing trouble.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki 'Rama to the Rescue' mushkil mein kya karna sikhati hai.
answer: When you are in trouble, stay calm and think quickly (presence of mind); a clever, safe plan can bring help, like the couple calling Rama the kotwal

subject: english
prompt_en: You are at home with your grandmother and you smell smoke from the kitchen. Using the story's lesson, what would you do?
prompt_hi: Tum ghar par Dadi ke saath ho aur kitchen se dhuein ki smell aati hai. Story ki seekh use karke tum kya karoge?
answer: Stay calm, get grandmother and yourself out safely, and call for help (a neighbour, or the emergency number 112); do not try to fight a big fire alone

subject: english
prompt_en: Write the full forms: 'I'm so tired tonight.' and 'They're still awake.'
prompt_hi: Poora form likho: 'I'm so tired tonight.' aur 'They're still awake.' Apostrophe kis letter ki jagah hai?
answer: I am; they are

subject: english
prompt_en: Find and fix two mistakes: 'Their awake! Ill call out softly.'
prompt_hi: Do galtiyan dhoondo aur theek karo: 'Their awake! Ill call out softly.'
answer: They're awake! I'll call out softly.

subject: english
prompt_en: Fill in the present progressive: 'Listen! Someone ___ (dig) a hole in the wall.'
prompt_hi: Present progressive bharo: 'Listen! Someone ___ (dig) a hole in the wall.' Abhi ho raha hai, toh kya lagega?
answer: is digging

subject: english
prompt_en: Find and fix: 'The couple talking about a name for the baby.'
prompt_hi: Galti dhoondo aur theek karo: 'The couple talking about a name for the baby.'
answer: A helper verb is missing: 'The couple are talking about a name for the baby.'

subject: english
prompt_en: Fill in softly or loudly: 'If the boy is in the house, I'll call ___. If he is in the street, I'll call very ___.'
prompt_hi: Softly ya loudly bharo: 'If the boy is in the house, I'll call ___. If he is in the street, I'll call very ___.'
answer: softly; loudly

subject: english
prompt_en: Add the right mark and name the sentence type: 'what is that noise'
prompt_hi: Sahi punctuation lagao aur batao ye kaunsa sentence hai: 'what is that noise'
answer: What is that noise? It is an interrogative sentence (a question).

subject: english
prompt_en: Some people call the village policeman a 'thaanedar'. What is the English word for this person?
prompt_hi: Kuch log gaon ke policewale ko 'thaanedar' kehte hain. English mein ise kya kehte hain?
answer: a policeman (police officer)

subject: english
prompt_en: The mahout gave Gajaraj food and a bath every day. Why was Gajaraj still sad at the start of the story?
prompt_hi: Mahout Gajaraj ko roz khana aur nahaana deta tha. Phir bhi story ke shuru mein Gajaraj udaas kyun tha?
answer: He had no friend to play with; the mahout was a kind caretaker, not a friend

subject: english
prompt_en: When the tired, hungry dog came into the stable, what did Gajaraj do? What does it show about him?
prompt_hi: Jab thaka-haara, bhookha kutta stable mein aaya, Gajaraj ne kya kiya? Isse Gajaraj ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
answer: He pushed some of his own food towards the dog; it shows he was kind and wanted a friend

subject: english
prompt_en: After Buntee was taken away, Gajaraj would not touch his favourite food. Why?
prompt_hi: Buntee ke jaane ke baad Gajaraj ne apna favourite khana bhi nahi chhua. Kyun?
answer: He was missing his friend Buntee and felt too sad to eat

subject: english
prompt_en: Stop after the farmer tells Buntee to go to his friend and takes off the rope. Predict what Buntee will do.
prompt_hi: Yahaan ruko, jab farmer Buntee ko dost ke paas jaane ko kehta hai aur rassi khol deta hai. Predict karo, Buntee kya karega?
answer: He will run straight back to Gajaraj at the stable

subject: english
prompt_en: Before running off, Buntee licked the farmer's hand once. Why do you think he did that?
prompt_hi: Bhaagne se pehle Buntee ne ek baar farmer ka haath chaata. Tumhe kya lagta hai, kyun?
answer: To thank the farmer and show love for him for setting him free

subject: english
prompt_en: A: 'They were friends because they were the same.' B: 'They were friends although they were very different.' Which fits the story, and why?
prompt_hi: A: 'They were friends because they were the same.' B: 'They were friends although they were very different.' Story pe kaunsa fit hota hai, aur kyun?
answer: B, because an elephant and a dog are very different but became best friends

subject: english
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child why the story is called 'The Unlikely Best Friends', and who else became friends at the end.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki story ka naam 'The Unlikely Best Friends' kyun hai, aur end mein aur kaun dost bane.
answer: No one expects a royal elephant and a stray dog to be friends, but they became best friends; at the end the mahout and the farmer also became friends

subject: english
prompt_en: Make opposites with un- or dis-: kind → ___, appeared → ___, touched → ___.
prompt_hi: un- ya dis- lagaakar opposite banao: kind → ___, appeared → ___, touched → ___.
answer: unkind, disappeared, untouched

subject: english
prompt_en: Find and fix: 'By evening, Gajaraj's food had remain untouched.'
prompt_hi: Galti dhoondo aur theek karo: 'By evening, Gajaraj's food had remain untouched.'
answer: 'had remain' should be 'had remained'

subject: english
prompt_en: Fill in the past progressive: 'Gajaraj ___ (munch) his food when the dog came in.'
prompt_hi: Past progressive bharo: 'Gajaraj ___ (munch) his food when the dog came in.' Kaam chal raha tha, tabhi kutta aaya.
answer: was munching

subject: english
prompt_en: Find and fix: 'Neither the farmer nor the mahout didn't see the tears.'
prompt_hi: Galti dhoondo aur theek karo: 'Neither the farmer nor the mahout didn't see the tears.'
answer: Remove 'didn't': 'Neither the farmer nor the mahout saw the tears.'

subject: english
prompt_en: Make your own sentence with 'neither ... nor' about two foods you do not like.
prompt_hi: Apna sentence banao 'neither ... nor' se, do aise khaane ke baare mein jo tumhe pasand nahi.
answer: A correct 'neither ... nor' sentence with no extra 'not', e.g. 'I like neither karela nor lauki.'

subject: english
prompt_en: A new student from Manipur joins your class. She speaks little Hindi and loves football; you love chess. What would Gajaraj and Buntee's story tell you about becoming friends?
prompt_hi: Manipur se ek nayi student class mein aayi hai. Woh thodi Hindi bolti hai aur football pasand karti hai; tumhe chess pasand hai. Gajaraj aur Buntee ki story dosti ke baare mein kya kehti?
answer: Being different does not matter; share, be kind, spend time together and find things to enjoy together

subject: english
prompt_en: Say it in English: 'Haathi ne kutte ko apni soond se uthaakar apni peeth par bitha liya.'
prompt_hi: Isko English mein bolo: 'Haathi ne kutte ko apni soond se uthaakar apni peeth par bitha liya.'
answer: The elephant picked up the dog with his trunk and put him on his back.

subject: english
prompt_en: In this poem, line 1 rhymes with line 2, line 3 with line 4, and so on. What do we call a pair of rhyming lines, and how do we write the pattern with letters?
prompt_hi: Is poem mein line 1 line 2 se rhyme karti hai, line 3 line 4 se. Do rhyming lines ki jodi ko kya kehte hain, aur pattern ko letters mein kaise likhte hain?
answer: A couplet; the pattern is AABB

subject: english
prompt_en: How does the speaker feel to have special friends?
prompt_hi: Special friends hone par speaker kaisa feel karti hai?
answer: blessed
